aboutMore: A few facts, since people have begun asking and one or two of you have been kind about it. I write obituaries for a small newspaper in Pawtucket, Monday through Friday, in a cardigan. It is exactly as grim as you imagine and a great deal kinder. I live with an enormous orange cat named Dorian, who has done more damage to my aesthetic than any glitter graphic ever could. My grandmother's coat hangs on the back of my bedroom door. I have never worn it. I only check that it is still there. I walk everywhere. It is practical. (She would be pleased.)

blog.title: Notes from the Obituary Desk
blog.body: I write obituaries for a living. People assume this is morbid. It is the opposite. A family calls, usually the same afternoon, and says: write something about my father. I ask what he liked. They say, he liked a lot of things. I ask for one. They say, the lake. Then they tell me about the lake for forty minutes. That is the obituary. I am only the person who types it. I have rules. No euphemisms except the ones the family chooses. Always the dog, if there was a dog. Always the name of the lake. Last month a man called about his wife of fifty-one years and said, 'She would not want a fuss.' I wrote six lines. He called back to say I had got her gardening gloves right. I did not know about the gloves. He had said it in passing, on the phone, and I had written it down. I do not think anyone has ever thanked the person who types the obituary. He did. I have been thinking about the gloves for a week.

blog.title: A Cat Named Dorian (An Aesthetic Crisis)
blog.body: I want it on the record that I did not choose an orange cat. I went to the shelter for a small, dark, serious animal, the sort that sits on a windowsill and judges the weather. A volunteer put Dorian in my arms. He is the color of a traffic cone. He weighs seventeen pounds. He has the face of a man who has never once been denied a sandwich. I said 'no.' He put his head under my chin. I filled out the paperwork. He is named for the Wilde novel, because I was in a mood, and he has spent every day since making a mockery of the allusion: the portrait in his attic, if he had one, would be of a sandwich. He knocks pens off my desk one at a time, at 3 AM, and watches me pick them up. I have bought a black bed, a black blanket, a black bowl. He sleeps on the white towel. He knows. The towel is the point. We have reached an understanding. Please do not send me pictures of other cats.

blog.title: I Was Asked to Name Three Songs
blog.body: I entered the mall store on the fourteenth, a little after four, which I do twice a year, for candles and for the pleasure of being mildly disappointed. The girl at the register, whose name tag said HOLLY, and whose eyeliner I would grade a B-plus, looked at the Bauhaus pin on my collar and said, 'Cute pin. Name three songs.' It is, apparently, a test they give. I said, 'Which three?' She said, 'Any three.' I named eleven. In order of release. I added a note on the B-sides. There was a silence. A customer behind me dropped a keychain. Holly said, 'Nobody has ever done that.' I said, 'You asked.' She rang up the candle and a notebook with an Edward Gorey ghost on the cover and applied the employee discount without being asked. As I turned to go I could hear, leaking from the headphones around her neck, something extremely cheerful with a key change. I said nothing. I will say nothing here either. I would only like it noted that I did not judge, and that the candle is lovely.

blog.title: My Grandmother's Coat
blog.body: My grandmother wore black for forty years. Asked why, she said it was practical. It did not show gravy. It went to every funeral without a second thought. It was, she said, one less decision. She was the funniest person I have ever known. She kept a wool coat, black, with a worn velvet collar, that she wore from October until the first crocus. It hangs on the back of my door now. It is too big in the shoulders. I have not worn it. I check on it, the way one checks on a sleeping person. Here is a short poem. It rhymes. I have allowed it, as an exception, for her. 'Her coat still holds the shape of cold, / the collar worn where hands would go. / I do not wear it. I just hold / it up against the door, and know.' She was right, by the way. It is practical. It is also the warmest thing I own, and I have never put it on.

survey.title: The Survey (Forwarded by Tina. Answered once, with reluctance, in full sentences.)
qa: Name:
Raven. The rest is on a driver's license in a drawer.
Age:
Twenty-four. Old for this website, young for my taste in music.
Occupation:
Obituary writer. Yes. People ask. It is the kindest job I have ever had.
Pets:
One orange cat named Dorian. I did not choose the color.
Favorite tea:
Lapsang souchong. It smells like a fire in someone else's house. This is a compliment.
Last book read:
Rebecca. Third time. Mrs. Danvers is the only character I fully trust.
Best concert:
A small room in Providence, forty people, a band nobody has heard of, and a man beside me who wept quietly during the second song. I remember thinking: good.
Biggest fear:
Becoming a person who says 'it was better before.' I am already close. I have met a warning on this site and he is perfectly nice.
Something you would never do:
Type 'rawr.' Wear glitter. Be late to a funeral. In ascending order of difficulty.
A secret:
I am sentimental about this entire website. The girl who reposts the chain letters. The boy and his rock. I would defend all of them in a court of law. Do not tell anyone.
Favorite season:
The week in October when the light goes orange at 4 PM and everyone briefly agrees with me.
Describe yourself in one sentence:
Punctual, dry, and a little warmer than advertised.

dms: Hello, malten. I have read your guestbook. Three of the entries say only 'asdf.' I replied to each one formally. One of them wrote back. We are now corresponding about the weather.
I read 'Why do we create?' three times. I have no clean answer. I will offer an untidy one: because the blank page is rude, and it is the only rude thing that will wait patiently for us to answer.
I clicked through your entire webring last night. Eleven sites. The last one links back to the first. I found that unusually comforting. A circle with no villain.
Dorian has learned to open the pantry door. He has not learned to close it. I now live in a house with an orange cat and a bag of flour in the hallway. Please do not ask what happened to the flour.
An obituary I wrote today mentioned a woman's parakeet by name and a man's lawn by temperament. I was proud of both. I do not tell people this at parties, mostly because I am not at parties.
It rained in Providence at three this morning. I stood at the window for ten minutes and counted streetlights. Seven. The eighth was out. There is always one out. I find that reassuring.

Someone on this site asked whether goth is 'just a phase.' I said it is a thirty-year phase and I am in the middle of it. They said 'cool.' I did not know that could be a compliment. I am still deciding.
I made soup tonight. Potato leek. I did not follow the recipe. It came out well. I am telling you because there is no one else awake. Dorian had a bowl. A small one.
I spent my lunch hour reading a headstone. It said 'Gone fishing.' I stood in front of it for a long time. I have not been able to improve on it.
A man on this site, a year older than I am, keeps saying 'back when we had testimonials.' I have started to hear myself in him. It is like seeing your own coat on a stranger.
repliesExtra: Noted, and appreciated, in that order.
I will think about that. I do not say that to everyone. I say it to approximately four people.
That is kind. I will pretend I did not enjoy it.
Your punctuation is excellent. I mention it because few people notice.
I read that twice. Once to understand it and once because it was nice.
It is late. I am answering anyway. Take that as a compliment.
Excuse any typos. A cat the color of a traffic cone is on my keyboard and does not accept feedback.
That is more charming than you realize. Do it again sometime.
Fine. You have my attention for as long as the tea holds.
statusesExtra: wrote six lines today about a man who loved a lake. the family said it was exactly right. that is the whole job.
Dorian has knocked a pen off the desk fourteen times. I have picked it up fourteen times. We both understand the game.
taking the long way home. it is raining. this is not a metaphor. it is Providence.
bought a candle at the mall store. was quizzed on Bauhaus. passed. do not make me do it again.
tea. rain. a cat the color of a traffic cone. the aesthetic holds.
stood in a cemetery at dusk and said nothing, respectfully, for twenty minutes. recommended.

wallExtra.text: ok so raven. my manager says ur the only person who has ever named 11. he wants to put it on a plaque. i said no. also u were right about the B-sides. also i'm not telling u what i was listening to. u know. u were there. thank u for not saying

raven hi!! gina here. i have ur cemetery rules in my notebook (numbered, dated): daylight, permission, ruler for scale, say hello at the gate, say thank u on the way out. the groundskeeper let me in. the recording might just say 'ok.' that's ok. (it was the wind. i wrote the wind down.)

Raven. You asked me to remove the testimonial. I have. I keep a copy in my text file, which is the same as keeping it in my heart, but searchable. Also: 'we are the furniture' is on a sticky note on my monitor. I would like it carved into something. -Fred

*luna pads up to the edge of the wall and sits, tail wrapped around her paws.* ...the pack read ur rain poem. ashfang (beta) says it is 'nice.' duskhowl (scout) says it is 'wet.' willow (the pup) cried a little. ((ooc: willow is my brother finn. he cried a little for real. he's 8. thank you.)) ((ooc: also is the orange cat real. my beagle pickle wants to meet him.))

~*~ raven someone showed me the one u wrote about the man and his lake. i read it at 11:11 and cried into my glitter. u r allowed to be soft. i won't tell. (i will tell no one. i will tell the moon.) ~*~

holly: Holly. The 'name three songs' test is a fine tradition and you should keep it. I would only add that the people who fail are not enemies. They are early. It is a long road from the first record to the third, and you were kind enough to let me through without a speech.
The discount was appreciated. I would not have asked. I would have paid, and been glad to. It is a good store. (I have said it. It will not happen again.)

For the record, I did not teach you Siouxsie. You learned her at a counter at fifteen from a woman who asked you to name a song. I was a customer. I am honored to be in the stockroom with you, spiritually.
gina: Gina. I read the retraction you are not retracting. Four hundred orb photographs, and 'they are pretty and I'm keeping them.' That is the correct position on dust. As for the cemetery: daylight, permission, scale, and hello at the gate are all correct. Add 'thank you' on the way out. The dead are, in my experience, very polite.

The voice in the balcony that says 'again from the top.' I listened twice. I would check the drama club's rehearsal schedule before the afterlife. If it is a ghost, it is a ghost with notes, which is the most theatrical kind, and I would be honored to meet it.
fred: Fred. I asked you to remove the testimonial. I did not say I had not read it. I printed it. It is in a drawer, which is the highest honor I have. A sentence of mine on a sticky note is, I find, the most flattering thing anyone has done with my writing. I am sorry I called you furniture. I am not sorry. It was kind.
Fred, please stop planning to leave. You are one of the only other people on this site who remembers dial-up as a physical sensation. I need a witness.
luna: Luna. The ribbon was a spare. I own two. I am glad it went to a cello case. Your teacher is right that it looks like a funeral and you are right that it is for a pack. Both things can be true. It is the whole subject of black velvet.
On your question to the council: yes. The answer is yes. I will not say to what. It stays in the inner den. Some questions are answered in private, and a wall is not a den.
